description.en: A short sample e-book on Indian Art & Culture — classical dances and music, monuments, festivals and paintings. Full chapter content will be added soon.
description.as: ভাৰতীয় কলা আৰু সংস্কৃতিৰ ওপৰত এটা চমু নমুনা ই-বুক — শাস্ত্ৰীয় নৃত্য আৰু সংগীত, স্মৃতিসৌধ, উৎসৱ আৰু চিত্ৰকলা। সম্পূৰ্ণ অধ্যায়ৰ বিষয়বস্তু অচিৰেই যোগ হ'ব।

content.en:
India has eight recognised classical dance forms. Bharatanatyam belongs to Tamil Nadu, Kathak to the north, Kathakali and Mohiniyattam to Kerala, Kuchipudi to Andhra Pradesh, Odissi to Odisha, Manipuri to Manipur and Sattriya to Assam.

Indian classical music has two main traditions — Hindustani music of the north and Carnatic music of the south. Hindustani music is associated with the gharanas and instruments like the sitar and the sarod, while Carnatic music is known for its compositions and the mridangam. The Natyashastra of Bharata is the ancient treatise on dance, music and drama.

India has several world-famous monuments. The Taj Mahal at Agra, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is a symbol of love built by Shah Jahan. Other monuments include the Qutub Minar and Red Fort in Delhi, the Ajanta and Ellora caves in Maharashtra, the Sun Temple at Konark and the temples of Khajuraho.

Festivals of India reflect its diversity — Diwali, Holi, Eid, Christmas, Bihu, Pongal and Onam are celebrated across the land. Indian painting traditions include the miniature paintings of the Mughal and Rajput schools, the mural paintings of Ajanta and the folk art of Madhubani, Warli and Pattachitra.
